chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And those whose hearts are to be reconciled.' He said: They are a people who affirmed the Oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and gave up the worship of those worshipped besides Allah, and testified that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), yet they were doubtful regarding some of what Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) brought.

So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, commanded His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) to reconcile them with wealth and gifts, so that their Islam might become good and they would remain firm upon the religion they had entered and acknowledged.

And indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) reconciled the chiefs of the Arabs from Quraysh and the rest of Mudar on the Day of Hunayn. Among them were Abu Sufyan ibn Harb, and Uyaynah ibn Husayn al-Fazari, and similar people among the masses.

So the Ansar became angry and gathered to Sa'd ibn Ubadah. He led them to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) at Al-Ji'rana and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, do you grant me permission to speak?' He said: 'Yes.' He said: 'If this matter of the wealth you distributed among your people is something Allah revealed, we are pleased; and if it is other than that, we are not pleased.'

Zurara said: And I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: So the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'O group of the Ansar, is all of you upon the word of your chief Sa'd?' They said: 'Our chief is Allah and His Messenger.' Then they said for the third time: 'We are upon the like of his word and his view.'
Zurara said: So I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: So Allah diminished their light, and Allah prescribed a share for those whose hearts are to be reconciled in the Quran.

key_terms.وَالْمُؤَلَّفَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ: And those whose hearts are to be reconciled
key_terms.وَحَّدُوا اللَّهَ: They affirmed the Oneness of Allah

ai.seo_question: Who are the 'Al-Mu'allafah Qulubuhum' and why did the Prophet distribute wealth to them?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that 'Al-Mu'allafah Qulubuhum' refers to early converts who had accepted monotheism but remained hesitant about the Prophet's message, necessitating financial incentives to solidify their faith. It highlights the historical context of the Day of Hunayin, where the Prophet distributed wealth to chiefs like Abu Sufyan, causing the Ansar to question the wisdom of this strategy. The narration concludes by affirming the divine establishment of their share in the Quran, a key concept in Shia exegesis regarding the political and spiritual dynamics of early Islam.
